prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2005 — Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and priorities
- Britain is heading in the wrong direction under Labour: too much tax and waste, poor public service standards, rising crime, and uncontrolled immigration.
- Conservatives pledge action focused on cleaner hospitals, disciplined schools, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes; more choice for individuals and power devolved to communities; and repatriation of some EU powers.

Economy, tax and pensions
- Cut £12bn a year in waste by 2007–08: freeze civil service recruitment, remove 235,000 bureaucratic posts, abolish/cut 168 public bodies.
- Use £8bn to reduce borrowing (avoid stealth taxes) and £4bn for immediate tax cuts.
- Spend at least as much as Labour on NHS, schools, transport, international development; more on police, defence, pensions; overall spending growth 4% a year (vs Labour 5%).
- Halve council tax bills for millions of pensioners (up to £500 per household) funded by central government; restore earnings link for the basic state pension; keep Winter Fuel Payment, free TV licences 75+, and the 2005 £200 council tax payment.
- Lifetime Savings Accounts with government top-ups; strengthen company pensions and use unclaimed assets to protect affected members.
- Keep Bank of England independence; no euro; deregulation via department “regulatory budgets” and sunset reviews; restore UK opt-out from EU Social Chapter.

Families, childcare and education
- Flexible maternity pay (6 or 9 months); up to £50/week per under‑5 child via Working Tax Credit, for any chosen childcare; support workplace nurseries and clubs for older children.
- Restore discipline: heads/governors control admissions/expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; protect teachers from malicious allegations; cut paperwork; money follows the pupil; simplify funding.
- Restore exam rigour; publish marks; allow international qualifications; slim National Curriculum; boost vocational routes with 300,000 grants for 14–16s.
- Two hours of after‑school sport; ban junk food; encourage trips with protections for teachers.
- Expand popular schools (600,000 new places first term); allow state-funded places at low-cost independent schools; moratorium on special school closures; FE reform; scrap university tuition fees and abolish Labour’s admissions regulator; grow endowments.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS funding by £34bn over the Parliament; abolish central targets; reduce PCTs, scrap Strategic Health Authorities; bring back matrons with ward‑closure powers for cleaning.
- Patient/GP choice of provider; funding follows the patient; protect viable community hospitals; contribution (half NHS cost) toward private operations to cut waits; aim to end waiting lists as known this Parliament.
- Partnership for long-term care so no one must sell their home; more support/respite for carers; reform NHS dentistry (monthly payment option).
- Health checks for non‑EU migrants; STI public health campaign.

Crime, justice and security
- 5,000 extra police officers each year; cut paperwork; elected police commissioners; zero‑tolerance neighbourhood policing.
- 20,000 extra prison places; honesty in sentencing (serve full minimum term); expand drug rehab to 25,000 residential places; reclassify cannabis to Class B.
- Homeland Security Minister; robust anti‑terror laws; controlled immigration integral to security.

Immigration and borders
- Australian‑style points system; annual overall immigration limit set by Parliament, including a refugee quota; asylum processed outside the UK; withdraw from 1951 Convention and modernise agreements; take back EU asylum powers.
- 24‑hour port surveillance; restore embarkation controls; create a British Border Control Police.

Accountability, devolution and communities
- Timetable for Action; ministers who fail to deliver lose jobs.
- Abolish regional assemblies; return planning/housing/transport/fire powers to local authorities; strengthen Parliament and select committees; cut MPs by 20%; English votes for English laws.
- Tackle illegal traveller camps; review Human Rights Act guidance; devolve arts/lottery decisions; extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Transport: modernise roads; review speed cameras (safety, not revenue); longer rail franchises.
- Environment: protect Green Belt; prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; lower VED for low‑emission cars; boost energy efficiency, renewables and recycling; ensure energy security.
- Rural: honest food labelling; Little Red Tractor standard for public procurement; CAP reform; strengthen animal welfare; free vote to overturn hunting ban.

Defence, Europe and foreign policy
- Spend £2.7bn more than Labour on front line by 2007–08; preserve regiments; improve procurement; save warships; NATO‑first cooperation.
- Remain committed to Iraq reconstruction; support Middle East peace (secure Israel and viable Palestinian state).
- Oppose EU Constitution (referendum within six months) and euro; restore Social Chapter opt-out; seek CAP and fisheries reform (repatriate control); support enlargement including Turkey.
- Meet 0.7% GNI aid target by 2013; increase UK control over aid; champion open markets, rule of law and democracy.

First-day/month pledges
- Day 1: set head teacher expulsion powers; set EU Constitution referendum date (campaign for No).
- First month: begin recruiting 5,000 extra police/year; bring back matrons; first Budget to cut waste and taxes; start 24‑hour port surveillance.
